ai.description: This small frog reaches 30 mm. It is brown with a distinct, pointed snout and a prominent, fleshy projection on the tip of the nose. It lacks a tympanum and has long, slender digits.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ingerana charlesdarwini* is uniquely identified by the distinct, fleshy, leaf-like appendages located on its eyelids, which are absent in other similar Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Ingerana charlesdarwini* inhabits the humid, dense evergreen forests of the Andaman Islands, typically found near rocky streams at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: *Ingerana charlesdarwini* is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to hunt for small invertebrates among the leaf litter of its forest floor habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ingerana charlesdarwini* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of approximately 30–40 eggs in terrestrial nests near water, where they undergo direct development.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ingerana charlesdarwini* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the state of Kerala at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Ingerana charlesdarwini* consists of a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps emitted from within leaf litter in humid forest habitats.
